style.vernacular: Highland valley capital (about 1,500 m) rebuilt after the 1917-18 and 1976 earthquakes: low flat-roofed or tile-roofed concrete and block buildings in painted render, walled compounds, arcaded colonial-era plazas with seismic baroque and neoclassical churches in thick masonry, and a tower and mall district in zones 4, 9, 10 and 14 clad in glass.
style.ornament: Seismic baroque and neoclassical church facades in thick lime-and-stone masonry; wrought-iron balconies and window grilles; Maya-inspired relief and sculptural forms (Efrain Recinos, jaguar and stepped-pyramid motifs); large murals on university and civic concrete; walled gated compounds.

sources.what: Valle de la Ermita at ~1,500 m, tropical savanna tempered by altitude, neoclassical cathedral 1782-1815, post-1917 earthquake grid rebuild, skyscraper districts with height caps
white Guatemalan marble temple, six spires, 1984
sculptural jaguar-shaped cultural centre by Efrain Recinos on the old Fuerte de San Jose
